newsitem.title: CANADA: Crystallex says court affirms its claim.
newsitem.headline: Crystallex says court affirms its claim.

text.p: Crystallex International Corp said on Thursday that Tuesday's ruling by the Supreme Court of Venezuela reaffirms Crystallex's position as to the validity of its ownership rights over part of the Las Cristinas gold property in Venezuela.
Crystallex said it will continue to seek "full recognition" of its ownership rights including through further proceedings before the Venezuelan courts.
On Tuesday the court ordered publication in Venezuela's Official Gazette of a notice of transfer of Las Cristinas 4 & 6 concessions to Inversora Mael, C.A. (Mael).
The ownership of the two blocks is claimed by both Crystallex and Placer Gold Inc, who hopes to begin building a mine there next month.
Trading of Crystallex's stock was halted on the Toronto Stock Exchange on Wednesday, fuelling speculation that Crystallex had positive news about its Cristinas claim.

"The current ruling reaffirms Crystallex's position as to the validity of its ownership rights to Las Cristinas 4 and 6 despite announcements by certain Venezuelan officials and Placer Dome questioning those rights," Crystallex said in a statement.

It said Las Cristinas 4 & 6 concessions were transferred to Mael in 1986. The publication in the Official Gazette is the final legal formality required under Venezuelan mining law to perfect the transfer for all purposes.

On Wednesday Placer said the court decisions deal with the procedural issue of whether notice had been published as required by law when the concessions were transferred from Ramon Torres to Inversora Mael C.A. and not with the issue of underlying rights of tenure.

Crystallex said the validity of the transfer to Mael had been confirmed by rulings of the Supreme Court of Venezuela issued in 1991 and 1996. It said the rulings also declared the nullity of resolutions of the Minister of Energy and Mines denying Mael's right to publication of the transfer in the Official Gazette and provided that the legal effect of the rulings is to be taken as of 1986.

The Supreme Court also ordered the publication in the Official Gazette of each of the 1991, 1996 and the current ruling as well as the assignment agreement through which Mael acquired the Las Cristinas 4 & 6 concessions.
